# We are now Cencora. Our shared identity unites us.

Cencora brings the companies and services of AmerisourceBergen together under one new name.

[ Meet Cencora ][86]
[A banner that says We Are Cencora on a pink and purple background]

# Marketplace gives pharmacies access to thousands of uniquely curated front-of-store products

We’re reimagining the procurement process by enabling pharmacies to source all the products they
need from front to back through one convenient platform.
[ Learn more ][87]
[A person viewing the Marketplace homepage on their laptop]

## We are united in our responsibility
## to create healthier futures.

As we pursue our purpose, we make a positive impact on the health of people and animals around the
world.

### Pharmaceutical distribution solutions

Our wholesale and specialty distribution services ensure that crucial medications efficiently,
reliably and securely reach their destinations every day.
[ Learn more ][88]
[AB_1Card_03]

### Manufacturer solutions

In addition to distribution and logistics, we help pharmaceutical manufacturers bring their products
to market – and assist with each step from pre-commercial and clinical trial to broad market
availability and patient adherence.
[ Learn more ][89]
[AB_2_3_Card_03]

### Provider solutions

Our solutions power patient care for pharmacies, physician practices, hospitals and health systems.
[ Learn more ][90]
[AB_2_3_Card_05]

### Animal health solutions

We deliver distribution, technology and innovation for veterinarians, livestock producers and
manufacturers to make a meaningful difference in their businesses and the health of animals.
[ Learn more ][91]
[GettyImages-907614352_JPG]

## In the news

Read the latest press releases and media mentions.
[ Explore newsroom ][92]

## Insights

Access the newest in thought leadership.
[ Explore insights ][93]

# Careers with purpose

With a global presence and 44,000+ team members strong, AmerisourceBergen is committed to making a
difference in the future of health.
[ Explore careers ][94]
[GettyImages-1178

# World-class science. Life-changing impact.

Get an inside look at the work we do every day to define what's possible and transform patients'
lives through science.

[ see what drives us ][68]

## Life + Science

[ view more stories ][69]

## Areas of focus
* [
  
  ### Oncology
  
  Building on our heritage in the treatment of solid tumors, we’re solving complex scientific
  problems for cancer patients everywhere.
  
  Learn more about Oncology ][70]
* [
  
  ### Hematology
  
  Known for delivering many transformational firsts in hematology, we’re committed to breaking new
  ground across diseases with high unmet need.
  
  Learn more about Hematology ][71]
* [
  
  ### Neuroscience
  
  We’re dedicated to championing the needs and experiences of people living with neurological and
  psychiatric diseases through disease-modifying and symptomatic therapies.
  
  Learn more about neuroscience ][72]
* [
  
  ### Immunology
  
  We’re working to deliver meaningful solutions that address unmet needs in dermatology,
  gastroenterology, pulmonology and rheumatology.
  
  Learn more about immunology ][73]
* [
  
  ### Cardiovascular
  
  Building on a 70-year legacy of paradigm-changing medicines, we’re leveraging our experience and
  expertise to take cardiovascular research to the next level.
  
  Learn more about cardiovascular ][74]

[ View more ][75]

* 50 Compounds in development
* 40+ Disease areas being studied

# World-class science. Life-changing impact.

Get an inside look at the work we do every day to define what's possible and transform patients'
lives through science.

[ see what drives us ][68]

## Life + Science

[ view more stories ][69]

## Areas of focus
* [
  
  ### Oncology
  
  Building on our heritage in the treatment of solid tumors, we’re solving complex scientific
  problems for cancer patients everywhere.
  
  Learn more about Oncology ][70]
* [
  
  ### Hematology
  
  Known for delivering many transformational firsts in hematology, we’re committed to breaking new
  ground across diseases with high unmet need.
  
  Learn more about Hematology ][71]
* [
  
  ### Neuroscience
  
  We’re dedicated to championing the needs and experiences of people living with neurological and
  psychiatric diseases through disease-modifying and symptomatic therapies.
  
  Learn more about neuroscience ][72]
* [
  
  ### Immunology
  
  We’re working to deliver meaningful solutions that address unmet needs in dermatology,
  gastroenterology, pulmonology and rheumatology.
  
  Learn more about immunology ][73]
* [
  
  ### Cardiovascular
  
  Building on a 70-year legacy of paradigm-changing medicines, we’re leveraging our experience and
  expertise to take cardiovascular research to the next level.
  
  Learn more about cardiovascular ][74]

[ View more ][75]

## Pipeline

AS OF APRIL 30, 2026
* 50 Compounds in development
* 40+ Disease areas being studied

Our pipeline targets areas where we can deliver transformative medicines — for patients who need
them most.

# Building a world of health around every individual

We connect people to the care they need, put medicine and wellness within reach, and drive greater
affordability, simplicity and convenience in everything we do.

## Combining our strengths for you

Health services Health insurance Pharmacy Prescription drug coverage

### Health services

We have an unmatched ability to reach people and provide them with access to the affordable, quality
health care and wellbeing services they need to live their healthiest lives.

[Explore our services ][110]

### Health insurance

Aetna® creates insurance plans that deliver a total, connected, affordable approach to health care.

[Discover Aetna plans ][111]

### Pharmacy

Our neighborhood pharmacies — as well as our prescription delivery and specialty medication services
— are making it as easy as possible for people to get the care they depend on.

[Visit our pharmacy page ][112]

### Prescription drug coverage

Our pharmacy benefit manager, CVS Caremark®, plays a critical role in the health care system by
helping to lower drug costs and expand coverage to the affordable medications people need to stay
healthy.

[Learn about drug coverage ][113]

### View transcript

Having 1 kid?...Not exactly simple.

Having 6 kids? Definitely not simple. Wait, that’s 8 people in one family. Whoa.

That means finding ONE tv show they’ll ALL watch.

Making ONE dinner they’ll ALL eat.

And how do you play a board game with 6 kids?…actually, that’s kinda simple.

Okaaay, not so simple.

But it’s not just tantrums.

It’s attitudes.

That’s right. Teenagers.

And how do you decide who gets the last piece of pizza?

But you don’t just have 6 kids, you have 6 kids all with chronic illnesses.

That means on top of it all, you have to manage over 50 prescriptions, medical checkups, and support
everyone’s mental health.

Luckily, you’re not alone…I mean Tricia, obviously YOU’RE not alone.

But you’ve also got CVS Health as your healthcare partner, to manage specialty medications, provide
walk-in appointments, and keep track of it all in the CVS Health app.

So, does that make everything…simple?

No. It makes it simple…er

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

### View transcript

Having 1 kid?...Not exactly simple.

Having 6 kids? Definitely not simple. Wait, that’s 8 people in one family. Whoa.

That means finding ONE tv show they’ll ALL watch.

Making ONE dinner they’ll ALL eat.

And how do you play a board game with 6 kids?…actually, that’s kinda simple.

Okaaay, not so simple.

But it’s not just tantrums.

It’s attitudes.

That’s right. Teenagers.

And how do you decide who gets the last piece of pizza?

But you don’t just have 6 kids, you have 6 kids all with chronic illnesses.

That means on top of it all, you have to manage over 50 prescriptions, medical checkups, and support
everyone’s mental health.

Luckily, you’re not alone…I mean Tricia, obviously YOU’RE not alone.

But you’ve also got CVS Health as your healthcare partner, to manage specialty medications, provide
walk-in appointments, and keep track of it all in the CVS Health app.

So, does that make everything…simple?

No. It makes it simple…er

And sometimes, “simpler” is all you need to live a little happier and healthier.

But who gets the last piece of pizza? That’s still your call.

When you need more than a pharmacy…
CVS Health.
Healthier Happens Together.

# We are Committed to Life

[More][106]
[

### Vision

We strive to transform Fresenius Kabi in the decade to come. We are committed to increase
efficiencies in the therapy and care of patients and improve access to high-quality healthcare
around the globe.

[healthcare professionals in action]
][107]
[

### Excellence

We are specialized in lifesaving medicines and technologies for critically and chronically ill
patients. With our passion and expertise, we touch the lives of almost 450 million people every
year, each one representing the importance of our work.

[healthcare professionals in action]
][108]
[

### Sustainability

We constantly strive to improve our sustainability footprint. For us, meeting the needs of patients
and healthcare professionals goes hand in hand with responsible and ethical management.

[nurse taking hand of woman]
][109]
[

### Think Beyond: Latest Evidence for Effective Therapies in CKD

Join experts at the Global Renal Nutrition Webinar on June 16, 2026. Explore ERA 2026 insights,
protein‑reduced diets, and targeted CKD nutrition.
[Global Kidney Nutrition Webinar Key Visual]
][110]
[

### Women Who Shaped Us

At Fresenius Kabi, colleagues worldwide share personal stories for International Women’s Day,
honoring the women who shaped their courage and purpose.
[Images of Fresenius Kabi employees being interviewed on international womens day.]
][111]
[

### Fresenius Kabi recognized as a Top Employer in 13 countries

Fresenius Kabi has been certified by Top Employers Institute as a Top Employer for 2026 in 13
countries and additionally two regions.
[Image showing the top employer 2026 seals of the 13 countries and 2 regions.]
][112]
[

### Four Colleagues, Four Scientific Journeys: Voices of Women in Science

Female scientists from Biopharma, MedTech, Nutrition and Pharma share their stories and advice,
showing how science careers impact patient care and innovation.
[Image of women in science.]
][113]
[

### Meet The Heroes Behind Patient Safety

Unseen heroes ensure patient safety through precision, care, and smart tech at Fresenius Kabi.
Discover how people make the difference.
[Several people in different job roles like production and lab workers depicted as heroes with capes
and gadgets.]
][114]

  * [Pharmaceutical, Medical Supplies & Products Distribution Services][53]
    
    We distribute pharmaceuticals and medical supplies to healthcare settings across North America,
    from pharmacies and hospitals to doctors’ offices and clinics.
    * [Pharmaceutical Distribution Services][54]
    * [Medical Supply Distribution][55]
  * [Pharmacy Services][56]
    
    We help to ensure the financial wellbeing of pharmacies and health systems and support a stable
    work environment for their employees.
  * [Oncology & Multispecialty Solutions][57]
    
    We provide research, insights, technologies and other support to help address challenges in
    cancer and specialty care.
  * [Biopharma Capabilities][58]
    
    We provide a suite of solutions designed to address access, affordability and adherence
    challenges by bridging the gaps between biopharma companies, pharmacies, providers, and payers
    to help patients get on and stay on their medications.
  * [Prescription Benefit Solutions][59]
    
    We offer solutions that enable employers, payers, health-plan brokers and government agencies to
    provide lower-cost options for prescription medications and therapies.
  * [Consumer Products & Services][60]
    
    We help to ensure the financial wellbeing of pharmacies and health systems and support a stable
    work environment for their employees.

# Advancing Health Outcomes for All®

[ Discover McKesson ][125]

## Making Healthcare Happen

McKesson Corporation is a U.S.-based company with approximately 43,000 employees worldwide and
facilities across the U.S. and Canada. We serve as the logistical and operational backbone of the
U.S. healthcare system, helping ensure patients can access the therapies and care they need when and
where they need them.

Business Solutions
 

## Our Areas of Focus

Our services and technology ensure medicines reach every care setting, bring cancer and specialty
care close to home, and help patients break through access and affordability barriers.

We’re reimagining what’s possible by accelerating clinical trials, helping patients start and stay
on therapy, and building a stronger, smarter supply chain for the future.

[ Learn More ][126]

setting.]

[A person in a yellow shirt and gray cardigan holds a smartphone and a pill bottle, with a child in

### [ Prescription Benefit Solutions ][131]

[Person sitting on the floor in a living room, wrapping a bandage around their elbow. A yellow

### [ Consumer Products & Services ][132]

[Worker pulls pallet jack quickly through a warehouse aisle, shelves lined with boxes, motion blur

Strengthening Healthcare
 

## Powering Care Locally

For nearly two centuries, McKesson has strengthened the systems that move care forward by supporting
providers, enabling access to medicines and therapies, and removing barriers across the patient
journey.

McKesson Corporation is a U.S.-based company with approximately 43,000 employees worldwide and
facilities across the U.S. and Canada. We serve as the logistical and operational backbone of the
U.S. healthcare system, helping ensure patients can access the therapies and care they need when and
where they need them.

Our services and technology ensure medicines reach every care setting, bring cancer and specialty
care close to home, and help patients break through access and affordability barriers.

We’re reimagining what’s possible by accelerating clinical trials, helping patients start and stay
on therapy, and building a stronger, smarter supply chain for the future.

Frequently Asked Questions

## Answers for International Patients

Our international patient advisors are here to help you, 24/7.

**Still have questions?** [Talk to an Advisor][77]
01What exactly does Acıbadem Health Point do for me?

We are your single point of contact for treatment in Türkiye — reviewing your case with the right
specialists, building a clear plan and estimate, and coordinating every detail from your first
question to your recovery back home.

02How do I start, and what does it cost to ask?

Share your reports or simply describe your situation. A specialist reviews your case and you receive
a tailored plan with transparent cost information. The initial assessment costs you nothing.

03Can I speak to a doctor before deciding to travel?

Yes. You can request a written second opinion or a secure video consultation with an Acıbadem
specialist, so you decide with full confidence before booking anything.

04Will I be understood in my own language?

A dedicated multilingual team and professional interpreters support you before, during and after
treatment, so nothing is lost between you and your doctors.

05Are the hospitals and doctors truly world-class?

Care is delivered in JCI-accredited hospitals by physicians recognised internationally in their
fields, using the same advanced technology and protocols you would expect from a leading global
centre.

06What happens after I return home?

Your treatment does not end at discharge. You leave with full medical documentation and a direct
line back to your care team for follow-up questions and ongoing guidance.

Frequently Asked Questions

## Answers for International Patients

Our international patient advisors are here to help you, 24/7.

**Still have questions?** [Talk to an Advisor][77]
01What exactly does Acıbadem Health Point do for me?

We are your single point of contact for treatment in Türkiye — reviewing your case with the right
specialists, building a clear plan and estimate, and coordinating every detail from your first
question to your recovery back home.

02How do I start, and what does it cost to ask?

Share your reports or simply describe your situation. A specialist reviews your case and you receive
a tailored plan with transparent cost information. The initial assessment costs you nothing.

03Can I speak to a doctor before deciding to travel?

Yes. You can request a written second opinion or a secure video consultation with an Acıbadem
specialist, so you decide with full confidence before booking anything.

04Will I be understood in my own language?

A dedicated multilingual team and professional interpreters support you before, during and after
treatment, so nothing is lost between you and your doctors.

05Are the hospitals and doctors truly world-class?

Care is delivered in JCI-accredited hospitals by physicians recognised internationally in their
fields, using the same advanced technology and protocols you would expect from a leading global
centre.

06What happens after I return home?

Your treatment does not end at discharge. You leave with full medical documentation and a direct
line back to your care team for follow-up questions and ongoing guidance.

### Welcome to Action Bladder Cancer UK

Action Bladder Cancer UK (ABC UK) is a national charity dedicated to improving the lives of people
affected by bladder cancer. We work to raise awareness of the disease, support patients and their
families, campaign for better services and outcomes, and fund vital research into new treatments.

We also work closely with health professionals to improve understanding and care, offering
specialist education and resources such as our annual Nurse Education Day. Whether you are a
patient, carer, or health professional, ABC UK is here to provide information, support, and a
community working together to make real change for everyone affected by bladder cancer.

[Read about our work][44]
Bladder cancer is not rare. Every year, over 20,000 people are diagnosed in the UK

### Welcome to Action Bladder Cancer UK

Action Bladder Cancer UK (ABC UK) is a national charity dedicated to improving the lives of people
affected by bladder cancer. We work to raise awareness of the disease, support patients and their
families, campaign for better services and outcomes, and fund vital research into new treatments.

We also work closely with health professionals to improve understanding and care, offering
specialist education and resources such as our annual Nurse Education Day. Whether you are a
patient, carer, or health professional, ABC UK is here to provide information, support, and a
community working together to make real change for everyone affected by bladder cancer.

[Read about our work][44]
Bladder cancer is not rare. Every year, over 20,000 people are diagnosed in the UK

### Caroline’s story

After spotting blood in her urine, Caroline was diagnosed with high-risk bladder cancer. At 51, she
had her bladder removed and is now determined to live life to the fullest.

# BCAN: Empowering Better Todays & More Tomorrows

### We advocate for better todays and more tomorrows for everyone impacted by bladder cancer by
### focusing on four critical areas: education, support, research and policy.

[Find Help Now][128]

## Understanding Bladder Cancer

### What is bladder cancer?

Bladder cancer most often begins in the urothelial cells that line the inside of your bladder.
Cancer occurs when cells in the bladder start to grow out of control. Most tumors develop on the
inner layer of the bladder. Some can grow into deeper bladder layers. As cancer grows through these
layers into the muscle wall, it becomes harder to treat.

[Newly Diagnosed? Start Here!][129]
Dr. Armine Smith

## Signs & Symptoms

### Learn the signs and symptoms of bladder cancer!
* Blood in urine (hematuria)
* Painful urination
* Urgent need to urinate
* Frequent urination
* Feeling the need (but unable) to pass urine

[Learn More About Bladder Cancer][130]

### What is bladder cancer?

Bladder cancer most often begins in the urothelial cells that line the inside of your bladder.
Cancer occurs when cells in the bladder start to grow out of control. Most tumors develop on the
inner layer of the bladder. Some can grow into deeper bladder layers. As cancer grows through these
layers into the muscle wall, it becomes harder to treat.

[Newly Diagnosed? Start Here!][129]
Dr. Armine Smith

### Learn the signs and symptoms of bladder cancer!
* Blood in urine (hematuria)
* Painful urination
* Urgent need to urinate
* Frequent urination
* Feeling the need (but unable) to pass urine

[Learn More About Bladder Cancer][130]

## Get Involved

### Why Bladder Cancer Support Matters
* An estimated ****84,530**** people will be diagnosed with bladder cancer in the U.S. in 2026.
* About 9 out of 10 people with this cancer are **over the age of 55**.
* Bladder cancer is the** 4th most common cancer in men**.
* **1 out of 4 bladder cancer patients are women**—and they have worse outcomes at every stage of
  the disease than men.

[Get Involved with BCAN][131]

## About Us

### A Community For People Impacted By Bladder Cancer

Have you been impacted by bladder cancer? We’re here to help. The Bladder Cancer Advocacy Network
(BCAN) provides patients with the critical information and community support they need to thrive
today – and champions innovative research and responsive national policy to inspire hope for
tomorrow.

[Learn More About BCAN][132]

## Stories

### Read Stories of Hope

Sometimes it helps just to know someone else understands your journey. Read stories of hope from
bladder cancer patients and caregivers.

### Vincent’s Story

At 48, Vincent Rossi faced colon cancer and aggressive bladder cancer simultaneously, enduring years
of difficult treatment and setbacks. His story is a powerful testament to resilience, determination
and refusing to give up.

[Read More][133]
{“DeviceAngle”:0.030267413705587387}

### Margo’s Story

After years of surgeries, setbacks, and life-changing complications from bladder cancer, Margo
discovered that survival itself could be enough reason to keep going. Her story is a powerful
reminder that hope doesn’t require certainty—only the courage to take the next step.

[Read More][134]

### Shannon’s Story

At just 35 years old, Shannon received a bladder cancer diagnosis. She opens up about her experience
managing this illness while continuing to work, highlighting its effects on her career, mental
well-being, and physical health.

[Read More][135]

We rely on the generosity of our supporters and the strength of our networks to keep BCAN’s movement
alive! Help us provide support, tools, resources, and more when you make a tax-deductible donation!

# BCAN: Empowering Better Todays & More Tomorrows

### We advocate for better todays and more tomorrows for everyone impacted by bladder cancer by
### focusing on four critical areas: education, support, research and policy.

[Find Help Now][128]

## Understanding Bladder Cancer

### What is bladder cancer?

Bladder cancer most often begins in the urothelial cells that line the inside of your bladder.
Cancer occurs when cells in the bladder start to grow out of control. Most tumors develop on the
inner layer of the bladder. Some can grow into deeper bladder layers. As cancer grows through these
layers into the muscle wall, it becomes harder to treat.

[Newly Diagnosed? Start Here!][129]
Dr. Armine Smith

## Signs & Symptoms

### Learn the signs and symptoms of bladder cancer!
* Blood in urine (hematuria)
* Painful urination
* Urgent need to urinate
* Frequent urination
* Feeling the need (but unable) to pass urine

[Learn More About Bladder Cancer][130]

## Get Involved

### Why Bladder Cancer Support Matters
* An estimated ****84,530**** people will be diagnosed with bladder cancer in the U.S. in 2026.
* About 9 out of 10 people with this cancer are **over the age of 55**.
* Bladder cancer is the** 4th most common cancer in men**.
* **1 out of 4 bladder cancer patients are women**—and they have worse outcomes at every stage of
  the disease than men.

[Get Involved with BCAN][131]

bladder cancer patients and caregivers.

### Vincent’s Story

At 48, Vincent Rossi faced colon cancer and aggressive bladder cancer simultaneously, enduring years
of difficult treatment and setbacks. His story is a powerful testament to resilience, determination
and refusing to give up.

### Margo’s Story

After years of surgeries, setbacks, and life-changing complications from bladder cancer, Margo
discovered that survival itself could be enough reason to keep going. Her story is a powerful
reminder that hope doesn’t require certainty—only the courage to take the next step.

At just 35 years old, Shannon received a bladder cancer diagnosis. She opens up about her experience
managing this illness while continuing to work, highlighting its effects on her career, mental
well-being, and physical health.

# We are part of Cencora.

And you are at the center of everything we do. 

Cencora brings AmerisourceBergen and all of our companies and services, including Besse^{®} Medical,
together under one new name. While we are expanding our network of like-minded pharmacists,
physicians, caregivers and healthcare continuum, our commitment to supporting your ability to
provide patient-centric care has never been more of a focus.  It’s business as usual while our full
transition unfolds over time.
[ Learn more at Cencora.com ][68]
[A light and dark blue gradient]

# Empowering community physician practices – one delivery at a time

## The specialty supplier that works in service of your business

You want to provide your patients with the best care possible. To do that, you need access to supply
and solutions designed for your practice’s unique needs. We tailor products, technology, and support
to your specialty. We provide fast, secure access to thousands of pharmaceuticals, offer smart tools
that optimize your profitability, and provide expert guidance on all your financial questions.
[ Our distribution services ][69]
[ Our industry leadership ][70]

WEBINAR: September 16th 2026, 12pm CT

## Medically Integrated Dispensing / In Office Dispensing for Specialty Practices

Whether your practice already has an established Medically Integrated Dispensing (MID) / In Office
Dispensing (IOD) program or pharmacy, or you are beginning to explore MID/IOD, Cencora’s Specialty
Practice Rx Services is hosting a webinar focused on operational and business considerations for
specialty practices.

Attendees will also learn more about Cencora’s pharmacy services and solutions, including Prime’s
IntegratedRx™ for MID/IOD and Elevate PSAO.

If your practice is evaluating MID/OID programs or seeking additional insight into dispensing models
and related considerations, we invite you to attend.


[ Reserve your spot today! ][71]
[doctor reviewing digital documents on a tablet]

Practice business analytics

## Uncover hidden revenue in your practice
## 

Your data may look strong on the surface—but missed billing, reimbursement gaps, and performance
variation can quietly impact your bottom line. InfoDive^{®} helps you bring those hidden insights
into view so you can make clearer, data-driven decisions about your financial performance.
[ Explore InfoDive ][72]

On-demand webinar

## Impacts for medically integrated dispensing in 2026 and beyond

During this webinar, our team shared insights into today’s medically integrated dispensing
challenges and how we partner with practices to streamline workflows and manage complexity with
confidence.

If you have any questions, please contact our team today.
[ Watch the recording ][73]
[ Connect with our team ][74]

On-demand webinar

## Keeping an eye on MIPS for retina practices

During this webinar, the MIPS consulting team discussed what MIPS means for retina practices in 2026
and how we partner with practices to simplify reporting and navigate program changes.

If you have any questions, please contact our team today.
[ Watch the recording ][75]
[ Connect with our team ][76]

Global Provider Insights Network® (GPIN)

# Participate in honoraria-based market research

Bring your expertise to a network of over 1,500 healthcare professionals

# Preparing for the Drug Supply Chain Security Act (DSCSA)

you don't need to feel overwhelmed. Use these resources to help you better understand what to expect
and how you can prepare.

# A 101 on the physician healthcare buying model

model for the physician class or trade.
[ See how we do it ][82]
[pinkpurpleblueabstract]

# Current topics for physician practices

[Calculator beside a pen and financial analysis paper]

Understanding the impact of the Medicare Physician Fee Schedule on your practice

The 2025 Medicare Physician Fee Schedule (MPFS) has introduced a new conversion factor of $32.35,
necessitating practices to assess its impact on revenue. InfoDive® reports provide insights on how
changes  will affect specific CPT Codes based on Medicare patient volume.
[ Read more ][83]
[ ]

The vital role of a distributor in the U.S. pharmaceutical supply chain

In this article, we’ll discuss the vital role of distributors in the U.S pharmaceutical supply
chain, their direct value, and how Cencora deploys this value to inspire positive change and empower
our provider customers to deliver the best care possible.
[ Read more ][84]
[People]

3 ways your distributor can help you prepare for DSCSA compliance

How your distributor should be investing time, talent, and capital to ensure you are prepared for
November 2023.
[ Read more ][85]
[12-18-2019-screen4_edited]

Roundtable discussion: How payer models and metrics can contribute to more equitable care

A conversation with Natasha Clinton, Senior Director of Medical Affairs at Cencora; Alexandra Chong,
PhD, Social Science Research Analyst at CMMI; and Angella Charnot-Katsikas, MD, Medical Director,
MolDx and Chief Medical Officer at Palmetto GBA.
[ Read more ][86]
[doctor with patient]

Recruitment tool pairs pharma firms with providers to boost patient connection 

Leadership at AmerisourceBergen talks to *Outsourcing Pharma *about Clinical Trial Navigator, a
suite of solutions designed to help clinical trials recruit with the help of community-based
specialty. 
[ Read more ][87]

# No matter your focus, we’re built to help

In order to best serve community practitioners, we’ve developed expertise across a broad range of
specializations. Regardless of your area of medicine, we have products and solutions that can help,
from the drugs your patients need to your financial systems to your business operations.
[ Find your specialty ][88]
[Vials of medicine]

July 2026

[ Learn more ][89]

July 2026

[ Learn more ][90]

July 2026

[ Learn more ][91]
[ See all product and industry news ][92]

## The power of partnerships

[Consultant and doctor with tablet computer]
Our network works with more than 1,500 manufacturing partners. As part of Cencora, our scale ensures
your practice has access to thousands of products at all times. We connect creators to caregivers,
helping our partners focus on innovation and giving your practice valuable options.
[ For manufacturing partners ][93]
[Consultant and doctor with tablet computer]

## Lifting the voice of community care

[Happy medical professional]

Community Counts is an advocacy initiative that represents community-based specialty providers with
CMS, with payers, with legislators and with patients.

By amplifying the voice of providers, our goal is to ensure that specialty care in the community
remains strong.

[ Community Counts ][94]
[Happy medical professional]

Cencora Foundation and Family Reach

# "A Financial Guide to COVID-19"

Free, downloadable guidebook for practices and patients, offering advice about managing the
financial struggles that often follow a serious diagnosis or job loss.
[ Go to the guidebook download ][95]
[Concerned family]

# Solutions for specialty and community practices

## GPO solutions

As the leading pharmaceutical distributor partner of GPOs in the USA, we help ensure access to the
lowest cost options and work to provide more contracting opportunities to every medical practice. 
[ GPO solutions ][96]

## Inventory management

Technology that strengthens your control of inventory and payment verification is essential. Our
cutting-edge inventory management solutions are designed specifically for specialty and community
practices.
[ Explore options ][97]

## Better ordering, tracking and reporting

Enjoy 24-hour access to order placement, order tracking, reporting and online payment management in
a streamlined user experience.
[ Learn more ][98]

# Get in touch

Want to learn more about our ordering platform, innovative practice solutions, or business approach?
We’d love to know how we can support your practice. Reach out and we'll start a conversation.

# Bladders Are Precious.

## They deserve to be handled with care.

[Next]
[
[A bladder-shaped icon]

### bladder cancer

Explore what's next in care

[
[An arrowhead icon that points to the right]

### The challenges in making
### treatment decisions

Navigate the evolving therapeutic options

[Down arrow]
][18]

## A vision for the future of bladder cancer

Non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) therapy has made great strides in the past few years.
However, with high recurrence and progression rates, there’s still room to grow.¹

[Take a closer look at an opportunity to advance care][19]
[A urologist speaks with bladder cancer patient and caregiver inside her office] Not an actual
patient-physician interaction.

## Did you know?

### For patients and caregivers

Understanding how a therapy is evaluated can help you and your doctor decide on the right treatment
plan for you.

[Learn the clinical terms that measure a therapy’s effectiveness and safety][20]

## A critical pathway in bladder cancer

Science has uncovered a key regulator in the underlying biology of bladder cancer.²

[Get to know the Rb-E2F pathway][21]

## Complexity of treatment decisions

Radical cystectomy. BCG. Novel bladder-sparing agents. Clinical trial enrollment. With a growing
number of treatment options for high-risk NMIBC, making the right decision can be complex and
challenging.

[Explore the therapeutic landscape][22]
[A uro-oncologist looks out a window as if considering bladder cancer treatment options] Not an
actual physician.
**References: 1.** Sylvester RJ, van der Meijden APM, Oosterlinck W, et al. Predicting recurrence
and progression in individual patients with stage Ta T1 bladder cancer using EORTC risk tables: a
combined analysis of 2596 patients from seven EORTC trials. Eur Urol. 2006;49:466-477. **2.** Wang
J-P, Jiao Y, Wange C-Y, et al. Rb knockdown accelerates bladder cancer progression through E2F3
activation. Int J Oncol. 2017;50:149-160.

## A vision for the future of bladder cancer

Non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC) therapy has made great strides in the past few years.
However, with high recurrence and progression rates, there’s still room to grow.¹

[Take a closer look at an opportunity to advance care][19]
[A urologist speaks with bladder cancer patient and caregiver inside her office] Not an actual
patient-physician interaction.

## Did you know?

### For patients and caregivers

Understanding how a therapy is evaluated can help you and your doctor decide on the right treatment
plan for you.

[Learn the clinical terms that measure a therapy’s effectiveness and safety][20]

## A critical pathway in bladder cancer

Science has uncovered a key regulator in the underlying biology of bladder cancer.²

[Get to know the Rb-E2F pathway][21]

## Complexity of treatment decisions

Radical cystectomy. BCG. Novel bladder-sparing agents. Clinical trial enrollment. With a growing
number of treatment options for high-risk NMIBC, making the right decision can be complex and
challenging.

[Explore the therapeutic landscape][22]
[A uro-oncologist looks out a window as if considering bladder cancer treatment options] Not an
actual physician.

and progression in individual patients with stage Ta T1 bladder cancer using EORTC risk tables: a
combined analysis of 2596 patients from seven EORTC trials. Eur Urol. 2006;49:466-477. **2.** Wang
J-P, Jiao Y, Wange C-Y, et al. Rb knockdown accelerates bladder cancer progression through E2F3
activation. Int J Oncol. 2017;50:149-160.

Prompt Service Delivery

personal telephone contact with a medical advisor in a matter of minutes to a few hours. Our medical
staff can draw up an individual medical program in up to 48 hours.

Generally agents require anywhere from 24 hours and up to 7 days for feedback to clients due to a
complex and slow medical tourism organizational system. They rely on external clinicians for advice,
so they cannot respond quickly. This distinguishes us from medical tourism agencies and establishes
a new standard.

If you contact a clinic directly, it may take anywhere between 2 - 8 weeks to receive a response to
your treatment request. Many clinics do not offer medical programs without personal, fee-based
consultations.

Independent advice and hospital selection

personalized, statistically based medical care programs and independent recommendations from doctors
and hospitals. As a renowned, global company, we provide responsible advice and stand behind our
recommendations.

recommended are often the same ones who provide the services. Consultations are provided by these
doctors, which calls into question their independence. Furthermore, clinics' rankings and quality
ratings are often not considered.

specializes in the necessary treatment. Often, only the treatments offered at that clinic are
provided. There is usually no statistical evidence of quality, which may lead to negative treatment
outcomes.

patients take when seeking treatment options. The process begins with an initial consultation,
followed by document and medical record preparation, program planning, and independent selection of

process.

model, which only includes booking treatment and interpreting services.

offered after discharge from the hospital.

pillars that take cancer patients from uncertainty to clarity."

### Comprehensive Medical Record Review

treatments, and current clinical condition to understand your case as a whole. This comprehensive

most appropriate next steps.

### Expert Second Opinion

stage, previous treatments, and molecular markers. These may include CAR T-cell therapy, TIL
therapy, gene therapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, proton therapy, and other emerging

their specific medical needs. We evaluate clinical expertise, treatment availability, institutional
capabilities, expected timelines, and other practical considerations so patients can make informed
decisions about where to seek treatment.

### Clinical Trial Matching and Access

We identify relevant clinical trials for patients with advanced, relapsed, rare, or
difficult-to-treat cancers, and we have particular expertise in accessing trials in China, India,
and the USA. Our team conducts an initial eligibility review, communicates with trial centers, and
guides patients through screening, documentation, and enrollment.

### End-to-End Care Coordination

From preparing medical documents and communicating with hospitals to appointment scheduling, visa
assistance, travel planning, admission support, and continuity of care, CancerFax coordinates the
complete treatment journey. This allows patients and their families to focus on treatment while we
manage the clinical and logistical details.

Our Difference

## Why Patients Choose CancerFax?

"We don't book hospitals. We walk beside families navigating the hardest decisions of their lives,
with compassion, care, and commitment that doesn't waver."

### Advanced Treatment Focus

Specialized expertise in therapies that are often inaccessible locally, cell therapy, gene therapy,
precision oncology, and clinical trials.

### Cross-Border Coordination

Comprehensive support across international treatment destinations, case review, admissions, hospital
communication, and logistics.

### Hospital & Doctor Navigation

Guidance on the right institutions, specialist matching based on diagnosis, and center selection
tailored to clinical complexity.

### Clinical Trial Awareness

Support in identifying and exploring clinical trial options when appropriate, including
mutation-specific and late-line investigational pathways.

### Compassionate Support

Human guidance for patients and families navigating difficult decisions, with emphasis on clarity,
honesty, and realistic, informed hope.

### Independent Second Opinions

Access trusted second opinions from global cancer specialists, ensuring every diagnosis, treatment
plan, and decision is reviewed with expert clarity.

Our Process

## How It Works?

A clear, structured, and compassionate four-step process designed to bring order to a difficult
moment.

1

### Share Your Reports

Upload your pathology reports, imaging results, treatment history, and any relevant clinical
documents securely through our platform.

2

### Our Team Reviews Your Case

CancerFax specialists conduct a thorough clinical review of your diagnosis, disease stage,
biomarkers, and treatment history.

3

### Identify Treatment Pathways

We explore suitable advanced therapies, clinical trial opportunities, and international treatment
options relevant to your case.

4

### Coordinate Next Steps

We help arrange specialist consultations, hospital admissions, additional diagnostics, logistics,
and ongoing care coordination.

countries.

### CAR-T Cell Therapy

CAR-T cell therapy is an adoptive cell therapy that genetically engineers a patient's own T-cells to
express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) — a synthetic protein that directs T-cells to recognize
and destroy cancer cells. First conceptualized by Zelig Eshhar in the late 1980s and brought to
clinical success by Carl June's group at Penn in 2010–2012, the first FDA approval (Kymriah for
pediatric B-ALL) followed in August 2017.

Learn more →][56][Treatment

### Tumor Therapeutic Vaccines

Tumor therapeutic vaccines are cancer immunotherapy treatments given to patients who already have
cancer, not to prevent it. They stimulate the immune system to recognize tumor-specific antigens,
mount a targeted T-cell response, and destroy cancer cells throughout the body.

Learn more →][57][Treatment

is first necessary to understand the nature of natural killer cells and their fundamental
distinction from the T-cells that are used in CAR-T cell therapy. The distinction between the two
types of cells is clinically significant in terms of safety, ease of access, and the types of cancer
targeted.

"Advanced cancer treatment guidance, clinical trial matching, and care coordination are three
pillars that take cancer patients from uncertainty to clarity."

### Comprehensive Medical Record Review

We carefully review your pathology reports, imaging scans, molecular test results, previous
treatments, and current clinical condition to understand your case as a whole. This comprehensive
assessment provides the foundation for identifying suitable treatment options and determining the
most appropriate next steps.

### Expert Second Opinion

independent medical opinion. The second-opinion process can help confirm the diagnosis, review the

important treatment decision is made.

### Personalized Treatment Guidance

We help you understand which advanced treatment options may be relevant to your diagnosis, disease
stage, previous treatments, and molecular markers. These may include CAR T-cell therapy, TIL
therapy, gene therapy, immunotherapy, targeted therapy, proton therapy, and other emerging
treatments. We translate complex medical information into clear and actionable guidance.

their specific medical needs. We evaluate clinical expertise, treatment availability, institutional

decisions about where to seek treatment.

### Clinical Trial Matching and Access

We identify relevant clinical trials for patients with advanced, relapsed, rare, or
difficult-to-treat cancers, and we have particular expertise in accessing trials in China, India,
and the USA. Our team conducts an initial eligibility review, communicates with trial centers, and
guides patients through screening, documentation, and enrollment.

From preparing medical documents and communicating with hospitals to appointment scheduling, visa
assistance, travel planning, admission support, and continuity of care, CancerFax coordinates the
complete treatment journey. This allows patients and their families to focus on treatment while we
manage the clinical and logistical details.

Our Difference

## Why Patients Choose CancerFax?

"We don't book hospitals. We walk beside families navigating the hardest decisions of their lives,
with compassion, care, and commitment that doesn't waver."

### Advanced Treatment Focus

Specialized expertise in therapies that are often inaccessible locally, cell therapy, gene therapy,
precision oncology, and clinical trials.

### Cross-Border Coordination

Comprehensive support across international treatment destinations, case review, admissions, hospital
communication, and logistics.

### Hospital & Doctor Navigation

Guidance on the right institutions, specialist matching based on diagnosis, and center selection
tailored to clinical complexity.

### Clinical Trial Awareness

Support in identifying and exploring clinical trial options when appropriate, including
mutation-specific and late-line investigational pathways.

### Compassionate Support

Human guidance for patients and families navigating difficult decisions, with emphasis on clarity,
honesty, and realistic, informed hope.

### Independent Second Opinions

Access trusted second opinions from global cancer specialists, ensuring every diagnosis, treatment
plan, and decision is reviewed with expert clarity.

Our Process

## How It Works?

A clear, structured, and compassionate four-step process designed to bring order to a difficult
moment.

1

### Share Your Reports

Upload your pathology reports, imaging results, treatment history, and any relevant clinical
documents securely through our platform.

2

### Our Team Reviews Your Case

CancerFax specialists conduct a thorough clinical review of your diagnosis, disease stage,
biomarkers, and treatment history.

3

### Identify Treatment Pathways

We explore suitable advanced therapies, clinical trial opportunities, and international treatment
options relevant to your case.

4

### Coordinate Next Steps

We help arrange specialist consultations, hospital admissions, additional diagnostics, logistics,
and ongoing care coordination.

Advanced Therapies

## Featured Treatment Areas

We cover the full landscape of advanced oncology, from cell therapies to precision radiation and
clinical trials.

[Treatment

### CAR-T Cell Therapy

CAR-T cell therapy is an adoptive cell therapy that genetically engineers a patient's own T-cells to
express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) — a synthetic protein that directs T-cells to recognize
and destroy cancer cells. First conceptualized by Zelig Eshhar in the late 1980s and brought to
clinical success by Carl June's group at Penn in 2010–2012, the first FDA approval (Kymriah for
pediatric B-ALL) followed in August 2017.

Learn more →][56][Treatment

### Tumor Therapeutic Vaccines

Tumor therapeutic vaccines are cancer immunotherapy treatments given to patients who already have
cancer, not to prevent it. They stimulate the immune system to recognize tumor-specific antigens,
mount a targeted T-cell response, and destroy cancer cells throughout the body.

Learn more →][57][Treatment

### CAR NK Cell Therapy

To grasp the reason behind the significant leap of CAR NK cell therapy over CAR-T cell therapy, it
is first necessary to understand the nature of natural killer cells and their fundamental
distinction from the T-cells that are used in CAR-T cell therapy. The distinction between the two
types of cells is clinically significant in terms of safety, ease of access, and the types of cancer
targeted.

# Uniting for a World Immune to Cancer

We bring people, science, and ideas together to advance cancer immunotherapy and expand treatment
options for patients.

[See How CRI Drives Progress][32]
Funders and supporters

## Power the Research

CRI connects passionate funders and supporters to the science that’s changing cancer care. You are
bringing tomorrow’s treatments to patients today.

[See ways to give][33]
Patients and caregivers

## Sharing Stories of Strength

Meet the patients and caregivers who inspire everything we do. Their journeys show how science,
support, and determination are helping more people survive cancer and thrive.

[Read their stories][34]
Scientists and researchers

## Lead the Next Breakthrough

CRI supports scientists and researchers with the tools to turn bold ideas into real impact. Through
funding, trial networks, and shared data, we help accelerate the future of cancer immunotherapy.

[Explore Research Programs][35]

#### Our mission is to create a world immune to cancer by driving scientific discovery, accelerating
#### collaboration, and turning breakthroughs into lifesaving treatments.

[Oswald at Carnaval]

### Oswald Peterson

Lung Cancer Survivor

## Funding Research That Saves Lives

With immunotherapy, Oswald went from barely standing to dancing in Trinidad’s beloved Carnival once
more.

[Watch His Journey][36]

Our Impact

## Turning Research Into Results

[Icon - funds]

Investment

$570M

$570M+ Invested in CRI research scientists worldwide

[Icon - science]

Results

30

30 cancers are now treatable with immunotherapy

[Icon - award]

Respected

Top 5%

CRI is highest rated among all U.S. charities

[Icon - people]

Patients

9M+

9M+ Patients benefiting from CRI research worldwide annually

[See Our Impact][37]
[Donate Now][38]

## Immunotherapy Success Stories

In these inspiring stories, patients, scientists and supporters share their personal experiences
with cancer. Their stories offer wisdom and hope to all those affected by cancer.

[Explore Immunotherapy Stories][39]
[Keith Doubman]

> “I’m hoping I’m really doing my part to one day find a cure or find a way to prevent cancer from
> impacting the lives of so many people.”

Keith Doubman

Funder & Supporter

[Hear from our Supporters][40]

Our partners

## Conquering
## Cancer Together

We cultivate lasting strategic partnerships with research institutions, cancer treatment centers,
biopharmaceutical companies, and nonprofits to facilitate innovation in immuno-oncology and advance
new lifesaving immunotherapies for more patients. 

[See all of our partners][41]

## FOCUSED ON THE FUTURE OF

## BLADDER
## CANCER

Passionate about developing and delivering bladder-sparing immunotherapies

[ Explore Our Pipeline Explore Our Pipeline ][47]
[A spotlight shines on a translucent bladder]

At **CG Oncology**, we envision a world where patients with bladder cancer live with dignity and an
improved quality of life. Through our pioneering work and unwavering commitment, we are making a
meaningful difference for patients and their loved ones—together.

# Our Science

## Cretostimogene
## grenadenorepvec

Cretostimogene is an intravesically delivered oncolytic immunotherapy (OIT) with a dual mechanism of
action. It has been evaluated in an extensive clinical development program, with data supporting its
potential to treat multiple types of non-muscle invasive bladder cancer (NMIBC). Cretostimogene is
an investigational drug and is not approved by any regulatory agency. Its safety and efficacy has
not been established.

disciplines of oncology, with a focus on innovative clinical and translational cancer research. The

translation of groundbreaking discoveries into tangible advancements in cancer care. Our platform

resources support an integrated multi-professional approach to cancer care, from a medical oncology
perspective.

its mission across oncology, worldwide.

# See what your competitors
# will do next.

While others chase press releases and earnings calls, we capture real intelligence from the data
trails companies leave behind unknowingly — whether competitors, acquisition targets, potential
partners, or emerging disruptors.

Book a Demo
[Watch the Walkthrough][7]
[From digital exhaust to predictions]

## Trusted by teams at

[Intuit][S2A][Eleventh Hour Group][Abridge]
The Problem

## Why traditional intelligence falls short
* Curated narrativePress releases, earnings calls, official announcements — that's the story
  companies want you to see. By the time something is announced, it's too late to respond
  strategically. You're reacting, not planning.
* Commoditized sourcesTraditional market intelligence pulls from the same obvious sources everyone
  else uses. If you're reading it, so are your competitors.
* Data without contextTraditional tools bombard you with notifications — a job posting here, a doc
  update there. You spend hours trying to figure out what matters. You have alerts, not answers.

How it works

## From digital exhaust to predictions

Each step compresses the input. Thousands of raw signals collapse into a handful of patterns, then
into a single forecast you can act on.
* Digital exhaust
  LinkedIn activity
  Job descriptions
  API documentation
  Web & copy changes
  Reddit threads
  + 19 more source types
  CaptureWe monitor the unintentional data trails companies leave behind — job descriptions
  revealing technical debt, API documentation exposing new features, employee posts leaking project
  updates and more. Intelligence they never meant to share.

  12 AE roles, 3 metros

  SynthesizeA single job post or pricing page tweak is noise. Hundreds, woven together, become
  patterns. We connect signals across sources — hiring spikes, doc changes, ad shifts, partnership
  chatter — to surface the combinations that actually mean something.
  Predictions
  Forecast

  enterprise launch

## Why choose Icon?

At Icon, we’re committed to delivering the highest quality care, close to home. We combine advanced
radiation technology with a team of experienced clinicians. We’re here to:
* Provide care grounded in international evidence and clinical expertise
* Deliver treatment that is safe, precise, and tailored to your needs
* Work alongside your existing care team to ensure a coordinated approach
* Work in partnership with [Nuffield][122][ Health][123] to deliver seamless, high-quality cancer
  care. Patients benefit from access to world class treatments, care from leading consultants and
  coordinated support from hundreds of specialists.

Our focus is on helping you move more comfortably and regain quality of life, supported by a team
who puts your care first.

## Smart Therapies for Difficult Diseases^{®}

### Our investigational immunotherapy products are tailored to each patient’s needs. We employ a
### “triangle offense” designed to deliver durable, complete responses in cancer and infectious
### diseases.

[Our Science][45]

At ImmunityBio, we envision a day when we no longer fear cancer, but are able to conquer it, thanks
to the biological wonder that is the human immune system. Our scientists are working to develop
remarkable new therapies that harness that inherent power by amplifying both the innate and adaptive
branches of the immune system, to facilitate the attack and elimination of cancerous or infected
cells today while building immunological memory for tomorrow. The goal: to reprogram the patient’s
immune system and treat the host rather than just the disease.

Dr. Patrick Soon-Shiong
Global Chief Scientific and Medical Officer,
ImmunityBio

## Investigational Immunotherapies

ImmunityBio is developing immunotherapies that activate both innate and adaptive immune responses to
treat cancer and infectious diseases. Our approach stimulates NK cells, T cells, macrophages, and
dendritic cells to create a durable immune response, aiming to outperform treatments like CAR-T or
checkpoint inhibitors.

#### Learn more about our therapeutic areas

[Bladder Cancer][46] [Glioblastoma][47] [Lynch Syndrome][48] [Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma][49] [Non-Small
Cell Lung Cancer][50] [Ovarian Cancer][51] [HIV][52] 

## ImmunityBio is continuously pursuing new immunotherapies designed to attack disease by
## *enhancing* the patient’s immune system, not weakening it.

[About Us][53]

## A Robust Clinical Pipeline

We are applying our science and platforms, including the development of potential cancer vaccines,
to treat cancers, as well as developing immuno- and cell therapies that we believe could sharply
reduce or eliminate the need for standard high-dose chemotherapy.

### Bladder Cancer

[Learn More][57]
Phase 2

### Lung Cancer

##### nogapendekin alfa inbakicept + Tislelizumab

**[Clinical Trials]** We have an established process, governed by regulatory authorities, that is
required for individuals seeking access to our Clinical Trials or approved therapies. Information on
our trials is available directly through our Find a Clinical Trial page on our website or at the
[https://clinicaltrials.gov/][66] ImmunityBio accepts no responsibility for any costs or charges
incurred as a result of fraudulent activity.

**[Recruitment activities]** We have an established process required for all positions prior to
issuing an offer of employment. The process requires formal interviews with members of our team and
never requires payments or fees from job applicants. We do not conduct interviews via messaging
tools like WhatsApp, Signal, etc. Qualified and interest candidates should apply to current openings
directly through our careers page on the ImmunityBio website. ImmunityBio accepts no responsibility
for any costs or charges incurred as a result of fraudulent activity.

In the event you receive a suspicious message – via email, WhatsApp, or text, etc. – we advise
against providing any personal information or paying any fees. If you have lost money or provided
your personal identifying information, please contact your bank and report the matter to the US
Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) via [www.ic3.gov.][67]

## Smart Therapies for Difficult Diseases^{®}

### Our investigational immunotherapy products are tailored to each patient’s needs. We employ a
### “triangle offense” designed to deliver durable, complete responses in cancer and infectious
### diseases.

[Our Science][45]

At ImmunityBio, we envision a day when we no longer fear cancer, but are able to conquer it, thanks
to the biological wonder that is the human immune system. Our scientists are working to develop
remarkable new therapies that harness that inherent power by amplifying both the innate and adaptive
branches of the immune system, to facilitate the attack and elimination of cancerous or infected
cells today while building immunological memory for tomorrow. The goal: to reprogram the patient’s
immune system and treat the host rather than just the disease.

Dr. Patrick Soon-Shiong
Global Chief Scientific and Medical Officer,
ImmunityBio

## Investigational Immunotherapies

ImmunityBio is developing immunotherapies that activate both innate and adaptive immune responses to
treat cancer and infectious diseases. Our approach stimulates NK cells, T cells, macrophages, and
dendritic cells to create a durable immune response, aiming to outperform treatments like CAR-T or
checkpoint inhibitors.

Cell Lung Cancer][50] [Ovarian Cancer][51] [HIV][52] 

## ImmunityBio is continuously pursuing new immunotherapies designed to attack disease by
## *enhancing* the patient’s immune system, not weakening it.

[About Us][53]

## A Robust Clinical Pipeline

We are applying our science and platforms, including the development of potential cancer vaccines,
to treat cancers, as well as developing immuno- and cell therapies that we believe could sharply
reduce or eliminate the need for standard high-dose chemotherapy.

against providing any personal information or paying any fees. If you have lost money or provided
your personal identifying information, please contact your bank and report the matter to the US

[Inven founders]
Ekku, Niilo, and Tommi
Co-founders, Inven

As analysts at McKinsey and BCG, we spent days searching for companies, piecing together ownership
and financial data, and rebuilding the same spreadsheets over and over again.

We thought there had to be a better way. In 2022, we set out to build it.

Since then, we’ve worked with 1,000+ M&A teams and spoken to thousands of professionals across
private equity, investment banking, consulting, and corporate development.

The core workflow is still the same — analyzing markets, finding the right companies, understanding
them, and reaching the right people. What’s changed is how it gets done.

That’s what we’re continuing to build: grounded in real data, shaped in close collaboration with the
teams doing the work, and evolving rapidly.

    chemotherapy medicine before surgery when you have early-stage NSCLC, which can be removed by
    surgery, **and** then continued alone after surgery to help prevent your lung cancer from coming
    back.
  * Each may be used with the chemotherapy medicines pemetrexed and a platinum as your first
    treatment when your lung cancer has spread ([advanced NSCLC][39]) **and** is a type called
    “[nonsquamous][40]” **and** your tumor does not have an abnormal “EGFR” or “ALK” gene.
  * Each may be used with the chemotherapy medicines carboplatin and either paclitaxel or paclitaxel
    protein-bound as your first treatment when your lung cancer has spread ([advanced NSCLC][41])
    **and** is a type called “[squamous][42].”
  * Each may be used alone as your first treatment when your lung cancer has not spread outside your
    chest (stage III) and you cannot have surgery or chemotherapy with radiation, **or** your NSCLC
    has spread to other areas of your body ([advanced NSCLC][43]), **and** your tumor tests positive
    for “PD‑L1” **and** does not have an abnormal “EGFR” or “ALK” gene.
  * Each may also be used alone for [advanced NSCLC][44] if you have tried chemotherapy that
    contains platinum and it did not work or is no longer working **and**, your tumor tests positive
    for “PD-L1” **and** if your tumor has an abnormal “EGFR” or “ALK” gene, you have also received
    an “EGFR” or “ALK” inhibitor medicine that did not work or is no longer working.
  * Each may be used as a treatment in adults for your lung cancer to help prevent your lung cancer
    from coming back after your tumor(s) has been removed by surgery and you have received
    platinum-based chemotherapy, **and** you have stage IB and your tumor(s) is 4 cm or greater in
    size, stage II, or stage IIIA NSCLC.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of skin cancer called [melanoma][45].
  * Each may be used when your melanoma has spread or cannot be removed by surgery (advanced
    melanoma).
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective in children with advanced
    melanoma.
  * Each may be used in adults and children 12 years of age and older with stage IIB, stage IIC, or
    stage III melanoma, to help prevent melanoma from coming back after it and lymph nodes that
    contain cancer have been removed by surgery.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective in children younger than 12
    years of age with melanoma.
* a kind of cancer called [head and neck squamous cell cancer (HNSCC)][46].
  * Each may be used alone in adults with HNSCC before surgery when your cancer can be removed by
    surgery, has spread to nearby tissues, and your tumor tests positive for “PD-L1,” **and** then
    continued in combination with radiation with or without cisplatin after surgery, **and** then
    continued alone to help prevent your head and neck cancer from coming back.
  * Each may be used with the chemotherapy medicines fluorouracil and a platinum as your first
    treatment when your head and neck cancer has spread or returned and cannot be removed by
    surgery.
  * Each may be used alone as your first treatment when your head and neck cancer has spread or
    returned and cannot be removed by surgery, **and** your tumor tests positive for “PD‑L1.”
  * Each may be used alone when your head and neck cancer has spread or returned, **and** you have
    received chemotherapy that contains platinum and it did not work or is no longer working.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of bladder and urinary tract cancer called [urothelial cancer][47].
  * Each may be used with the medicine enfortumab vedotin in adults when your bladder or urinary
    tract cancer has spread or cannot be removed by surgery ([locally advanced or metastatic
    urothelial cancer][48]).
  * Each may be used alone when your bladder or urinary tract cancer has spread or cannot be removed
    by surgery ([locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer][49]), **and** you are not able to
    receive chemotherapy that contains platinum (medicines called either cisplatin or carboplatin).
  * Each may be used alone when your bladder or urinary tract cancer has spread or cannot be removed
    by surgery ([locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer][50]), **and** you have received
    chemotherapy that contains platinum, and it did not work or is no longer working.
  * Each may be used with the medicine enfortumab vedotin in adults before and after the surgical
    removal of your bladder when your bladder cancer has spread into the muscle layer of the bladder
    ([muscle invasive bladder cancer [MIBC]][51]) but not to other parts of the body, **and** you
    are not able to receive chemotherapy that contains cisplatin.
  * Each may be used alone when your cancer has not spread to nearby tissue in the bladder, but is
    at high-risk for spreading ([high-risk, non-muscle invasive bladder cancer [NMIBC]][52]) and
    when your tumor is a type called “carcinoma in situ” (CIS), **and** you have tried treatment
    with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) and it did not work, **and** you are not able to or have
    decided not to have surgery to remove your bladder.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of cancer that is shown by a laboratory test to be a microsatellite instability-high
  (MSI‑H) or a mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) solid tumor. Each may be used in adults to treat:
  * cancer that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery (advanced cancer), **and**
  * has progressed following treatment, and you have no satisfactory treatment options.

  * has been shown by a laboratory test to be microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch
    repair deficient (dMMR).
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.

    * is HER2-negative, **and** your tumor tests positive for “PD-L1,” **and**
    * has spread or cannot be removed by surgery (advanced gastric cancer).
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for this use in children.

  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.

# FDA-APPROVED TO TREAT CERTAIN TYPES OF CANCER, INCLUDING CERTAIN EARLY-STAGE AND ADVANCED CANCERS

ONE OF THOSE CANCERS IS EARLY-STAGE
NON—SMALL CELL LUNG CANCER (NSCLC)

IT’S TRU.
KEYTRUDA & KEYTRUDA QLEX.

## Explore KEYTRUDA QLEX, a treatment for certain cancers given in 1 or 2 minutes*

KEYTRUDA QLEX is a subcutaneous injection given just under the skin by your healthcare provider in
**1 minute* every 3 weeks or 2 minutes* every 6 weeks** in the stomach area or thigh. Your dosing
schedule depends on the treatment plan your doctor prescribes.

Injection time only. Not total appointment time.
[Get to know KEYTRUDA QLEX][33]

## Get started by selecting a type of cancer

Select a cancer type

#### Understanding immunotherapy

KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are immunotherapies. Learn how they work with your immune system.

[How treatment works][34]

#### Side effects

Side effects may occur while taking KEYTRUDA or KEYTRUDA QLEX. Consult your doctor right away if you
experience any.

[Side effects][35]

#### Resources & Support

Explore our library of downloadable resources to help you in every step of your treatment journey.

[Patient and caregiver resource library][36]

### FDA-approved

## Ask your doctor about KEYTRUDA QLEX, an FDA-approved injectable immunotherapy

Given just under the skin as a subcutaneous injection by your healthcare provider in the stomach
area or thigh, KEYTRUDA QLEX can be administered in as little as 1 minute* every 3 weeks or 2
minutes* every 6 weeks. Your dosing schedule depends on the treatment plan your doctor prescribes.

*Injection time only. Not total appointment time.

[Get to know KEYTRUDA QLEX][37]

See Indications

KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are prescription medicines used to treat:
* a kind of lung cancer called [ non–small cell lung cancer (NSCLC)][38].
  * Each may be used in combination with chemotherapy that contains platinum and another
    chemotherapy medicine before surgery when you have early-stage NSCLC, which can be removed by
    surgery, **and** then continued alone after surgery to help prevent your lung cancer from coming
    back.
  * Each may be used with the chemotherapy medicines pemetrexed and a platinum as your first
    treatment when your lung cancer has spread ([advanced NSCLC][39]) **and** is a type called
    “[nonsquamous][40]” **and** your tumor does not have an abnormal “EGFR” or “ALK” gene.
  * Each may be used with the chemotherapy medicines carboplatin and either paclitaxel or paclitaxel
    protein-bound as your first treatment when your lung cancer has spread ([advanced NSCLC][41])
    **and** is a type called “[squamous][42].”
  * Each may be used alone as your first treatment when your lung cancer has not spread outside your
    chest (stage III) and you cannot have surgery or chemotherapy with radiation, **or** your NSCLC
    has spread to other areas of your body ([advanced NSCLC][43]), **and** your tumor tests positive
    for “PD‑L1” **and** does not have an abnormal “EGFR” or “ALK” gene.
  * Each may also be used alone for [advanced NSCLC][44] if you have tried chemotherapy that
    contains platinum and it did not work or is no longer working **and**, your tumor tests positive
    for “PD-L1” **and** if your tumor has an abnormal “EGFR” or “ALK” gene, you have also received
    an “EGFR” or “ALK” inhibitor medicine that did not work or is no longer working.
  * Each may be used as a treatment in adults for your lung cancer to help prevent your lung cancer
    from coming back after your tumor(s) has been removed by surgery and you have received
    platinum-based chemotherapy, **and** you have stage IB and your tumor(s) is 4 cm or greater in
    size, stage II, or stage IIIA NSCLC.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of skin cancer called [melanoma][45].
  * Each may be used when your melanoma has spread or cannot be removed by surgery (advanced
    melanoma).
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective in children with advanced
    melanoma.
  * Each may be used in adults and children 12 years of age and older with stage IIB, stage IIC, or
    stage III melanoma, to help prevent melanoma from coming back after it and lymph nodes that
    contain cancer have been removed by surgery.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective in children younger than 12
    years of age with melanoma.
* a kind of cancer called [head and neck squamous cell cancer (HNSCC)][46].
  * Each may be used alone in adults with HNSCC before surgery when your cancer can be removed by
    surgery, has spread to nearby tissues, and your tumor tests positive for “PD-L1,” **and** then
    continued in combination with radiation with or without cisplatin after surgery, **and** then
    continued alone to help prevent your head and neck cancer from coming back.
  * Each may be used with the chemotherapy medicines fluorouracil and a platinum as your first
    treatment when your head and neck cancer has spread or returned and cannot be removed by
    surgery.
  * Each may be used alone as your first treatment when your head and neck cancer has spread or
    returned and cannot be removed by surgery, **and** your tumor tests positive for “PD‑L1.”
  * Each may be used alone when your head and neck cancer has spread or returned, **and** you have
    received chemotherapy that contains platinum and it did not work or is no longer working.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of bladder and urinary tract cancer called [urothelial cancer][47].
  * Each may be used with the medicine enfortumab vedotin in adults when your bladder or urinary
    tract cancer has spread or cannot be removed by surgery ([locally advanced or metastatic
    urothelial cancer][48]).
  * Each may be used alone when your bladder or urinary tract cancer has spread or cannot be removed
    by surgery ([locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer][49]), **and** you are not able to
    receive chemotherapy that contains platinum (medicines called either cisplatin or carboplatin).
  * Each may be used alone when your bladder or urinary tract cancer has spread or cannot be removed
    by surgery ([locally advanced or metastatic urothelial cancer][50]), **and** you have received
    chemotherapy that contains platinum, and it did not work or is no longer working.
  * Each may be used with the medicine enfortumab vedotin in adults before and after the surgical
    removal of your bladder when your bladder cancer has spread into the muscle layer of the bladder
    ([muscle invasive bladder cancer [MIBC]][51]) but not to other parts of the body, **and** you
    are not able to receive chemotherapy that contains cisplatin.
  * Each may be used alone when your cancer has not spread to nearby tissue in the bladder, but is
    at high-risk for spreading ([high-risk, non-muscle invasive bladder cancer [NMIBC]][52]) and
    when your tumor is a type called “carcinoma in situ” (CIS), **and** you have tried treatment
    with Bacillus Calmette-Guerin (BCG) and it did not work, **and** you are not able to or have
    decided not to have surgery to remove your bladder.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of cancer that is shown by a laboratory test to be a microsatellite instability-high
  (MSI‑H) or a mismatch repair deficient (dMMR) solid tumor. Each may be used in adults to treat:
  * cancer that has spread or cannot be removed by surgery (advanced cancer), **and**
  * has progressed following treatment, and you have no satisfactory treatment options.
  * KEYTRUDA also may be used to treat children with this kind of cancer, and KEYTRUDA QLEX also may
    be used to treat children 12 years and older.
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA QLEX is safe and effective for this use in children younger than 12
    years of age.
* a kind of cancer called colon or rectal cancer. Each may be used when your cancer:
  * has spread or cannot be removed by surgery ([advanced colon or rectal cancer][53]), **and**
  * has been shown by a laboratory test to be microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) or mismatch
    repair deficient (dMMR).
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of stomach cancer called [gastric or gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) adenocarcinoma][54].
  * Each may be used in adults in combination with fluoropyrimidine and platinum chemotherapy as
    your first treatment when your stomach cancer:
    * is HER2-negative, **and** your tumor tests positive for “PD-L1,” **and**
    * has spread or cannot be removed by surgery (advanced gastric cancer).
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for this use in children.
* a kind of cancer called [esophageal or certain gastroesophageal junction (GEJ) carcinomas][55]
  that cannot be cured by surgery or a combination of chemotherapy and radiation therapy.
  * Each may be used in combination with platinum- and fluoropyrimidine-based chemotherapy medicines
    when your tumor tests positive for “PD-L1.”
  * Each may be used alone when:
    * you have received one or more types of treatment, and it did not work or it is no longer
      working, **and**
    * your tumor is a type called “squamous,” **and**
    * your tumor tests positive for “PD-L1.”
  * It is not known if KEYTRUDA and KEYTRUDA QLEX are safe and effective for these uses in children.
* a kind of cancer called [cervical cancer][56].
  * Each may be used with chemotherapy and radiation therapy when your cervical cancer has spread
    nearby to the lower part of your vagina or to pelvic organs or has affected your kidneys (Stage
    III to IVA FIGO 2014 classification).
  * Each may be used with chemotherapy medicines, with or without the medicine bevacizumab, when:

**A Diagnosis Unlike Any Other**

**Deserves a Pharmacy Unlike Any Other**

 

As a specialty pharmacy that is 100% focused on oncology, our mission is to improve the lives of
patients battling cancer. We have robust access to limited distribution oncology medications along
with personalized services such as financial assistance sourcing, expert clinical counseling,
insurance benefit verification, and digital support. We are an oncology specialty pharmacy with
Board-Certified Oncology Pharmacists and nurses with specialized teams to guide patients with
compassion and care along their cancer journey.

we focus all our efforts and resources on delivering meaningful advances for patients with
urological cancers.

There is a growing trend toward precision medicine and precision diagnostics in uro-oncology. Find
our expertise in bladder cancer diagnostics focused in this array of transformative solutions,
aiming to provide physicians with the right information at the right time, to inform more
personalized decisions on how best to manage each individual patient.
